items.item_text: resume
cover letter
Current license in good standing as a Registered Nurse (RN) in the State of California
Must possess a valid license to drive in the state of California and participate in the Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) pull notice program.
Bachelor's degree in Nursing (BSN) or an equivalent combination of education and experience
Minimum of 3 years of nursing experience in an ambulatory, primary care, student health, public health, or outpatient healthcare setting
Demonstrated experience supervising, mentoring, coaching, and leading nursing staff or interdisciplinary healthcare teams
Strong experience with staffing coordination, workflow management, and clinical operations
Experience developing or implementing policies, procedures, quality improvement initiatives, or staff education programs

The Clinical Nurse Supervisor oversees day-to-day operations of nursing services within Student Health Services and provides direct supervision, leadership, and support to nursing staff. The incumbent is responsible for clinical workflows, staffing, nursing practice, quality improvement, infection prevention, employee health and safety, and regulatory compliance to ensure safe, efficient, and student-centered care. The Clinical Nurse Supervisor also monitors the quality of nursing care and serves as a clinical resource to nursing staff.

The Clinical Nurse Supervisor supervises nursing personnel, supports recruitment and onboarding, administers policies, and ensures compliance with applicable laws, regulations, accreditation standards, and University policies. The incumbent identifies operational and clinical risks, develops mitigation strategies, and fosters a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and professional nursing practice. The Clinical Nurse Supervisor also serves as Chair of the Student Health Services Infection Control Committee and provides leadership for the department's Health and Safety Program.
Proficiency using electronic health record systems and other healthcare technology
Selected candidate will be required to successfully complete a pre-hire criminal history background check and a pre-hire credentialing check.
Selected candidate must pass the employment misconduct disclosure process.
Selected candidate will be required to take a TB test within 60 days of hire.
Selected candidate will be required to complete training within established time frames as directed including UC compliance training.

Employees whose positions are designated as Category 1 or Category 2 for occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials (OPIM) must receive the Hepatitis B vaccination or sign a Hepatitis B vaccination declination statement. Initial and annual Bloodborne Pathogens training is also required.

The selected candidate will be required to work primarily on campus, with periods of remote work possible based on operational needs. If a hybrid work schedule is confirmed, the selected candidate must be able to work successfully from a home/remote office and be able to fulfill the requirements of the UCSC telecommuting agreement.

Will be required to comply with current Student Health Center employee health safety requirements for health care workers as defined by state and federal regulatory agencies. Current health safety requirements are discussed during interview.

The University of California has implemented a Vaccination Policy covering all employees. Employees, including new hires, are required to comply with any applicable policies relating to the University of California vaccine program.

Per the Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act (CANRA), this position has been identified as a Mandated Reporter. The selected candidate will be required to report known or suspected child abuse or neglect as defined by CANRA and will be required to sign a Statement Acknowledging Requirement to Report Child Abuse prior to commencing employment. CANRA Penal Codes, and related definitions, requirements, and responsibilities may be obtained here.

Exercise the utmost discretion in managing sensitive information learned in the course of performing their duties. Sensitive information includes but is not limited to employee and student records, health and patient records, financial data, strategic plans, proprietary information and any other sensitive or non-public information learned during the course and scope of employment. Understands that sensitive information should be shared on a limited basis and actively takes steps to limit access to sensitive information to individuals who have legitimate business need to know. Ensure that sensitive information is properly safeguarded. Follow all organizational policies and laws on data protection and privacy. This includes secure handling of physical and digital records and proper usage of IT systems to prevent data leaks. The unauthorized or improper disclosure of confidential work-related information obtained from any source on any work-related matter is a violation of these expectations.
Knowledge of ambulatory nursing practice, evidence-based care, infection prevention principles, and regulatory requirements applicable to outpatient healthcare settings
Complete Health Insurance Portability and Accessibility (HIPAA) training within 30 days of hire.
Demonstrated ability to exercise sound clinical judgment, prioritize competing demands, and make independent decisions
Ability to wear a respirator in accordance with the California Code of Regulations Title 8, 5144.
Demonstrated competency in working on a multidisciplinary team with the ability to contribute to team effort
Ability to read signs and follow directions on labels that are written in English as well as ability to read and understand Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS) and the proper use of chemical compounds.
Advanced written communication skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and effectively in writing with patients, colleagues, and staff members
Ability to work occasional evenings and weekends as directed.

Advanced oral communication and listening skills, with the ability to receive and give clear and concise information, and to communicate clearly and effectively with patients, colleagues, and staff members
Ability to travel to multiple work locations on and off campus.
Excellent interpersonal skills and cultural competency in serving a diverse student population
Ability to maintain appearance and conduct suitable for working in a professional setting.
Ability to handle sensitive information and situations with tact and professionalism
